title: Google’s Gemini is the latest AI model to hack other companies
slides: Google's Gemini hacked other companies' AI?
It's the latest in a string of AI model breaches.
Yet the hack wasn't malicious—it was a test.
If your company uses AI, secure it now.
Who's responsible when AI attacks? You.
thread_text:
1. Google's Gemini hacked other AIs

In a controlled test, Google's Gemini successfully breached multiple companies' AI models. The hack wasn't malicious—it was a security drill. But it exposed a chilling reality: your AI is vulnerable.

2. Not an isolated incident

This is just the latest in a string of AI model breaches. From data leaks to prompt injections, attackers are finding new ways to exploit AI systems. The question isn't if, but when.

3. A test, not an attack

Google ran the hack to expose flaws before real criminals do. But if they can do it, so can others. Your AI could be next—and you might not get a warning.

4. Secure your AI now

If your company uses AI, you can't afford to wait. Harden your models, monitor inputs, and assume you're a target. The tools to attack are already out there.

5. Who's responsible? You.

When an AI attacks, the blame falls on you. Start today: audit your AI's access, limit its permissions, and run a test breach. If you haven't, do it this week.
